claim: The order-three Dirac operator l.bl.n is present in exactly 32 of the 87 models, and those 32 are precisely the ones that FAIL doublet-triplet splitting -- overlap zero, checked model by model, with the order-three top Yukawa as a control non-zero in 87 of 87. So the sector condition trades doublet-triplet splitting and an R-parity-clean spectrum against realistic neutrino masses: the 55 solvers predict m_nu ~ 4e-4 eV, 125 times too light, while the 32 others predict 5.6e-3 eV, within a factor of nine of the observed 0.05 eV. No model gets both.
mu_reading: generic mu is 3.4e16 GeV (order four) or 1.3e17 GeV (order three) against the ~1e3 GeV needed -- too large by 1e13 to 1e14 in every model. That is the quantitative form of the mu problem here.
prediction: dimension-four and dimension-five operators are absent, and dimension-six X,Y exchange gives tau_p ~ 5e39 to 1e42 years against a Hyper-Kamiokande reach near 1e35. The class predicts NO proton decay from any channel. If proton decay is observed, the class is dead -- the cheapest way to kill the construction.
what_is_exact: the set equality between the order-three Dirac models and the non-solvers. The masses and lifetimes are order-of-magnitude estimates with order-one coefficients assumed; the RATIO 125 to 9 comes from a measured difference in operator order and is robust, the absolute values are not.
status: operator orders dumped by the orbifolder with a non-vacuous control; the FI scale from its own D0_FI_term; the scales and lifetimes computed here
scope: N = 27 right-handed neutrinos measured on the flagship only and assumed for both classes; the proton lifetime uses the standard dimension-six formula with M_X at the compactification scale, where the Wilson line breaks SU(5) here. Inputs g = 0.7, M_s = 5e17 GeV, v = 174 GeV, alpha_GUT = 1/24.
